# Travel Planner API

> An API-first travel planner. The web app uses only this public API, so anything a person can
> do in the UI, an agent can do here too. The full machine-readable contract is /openapi.json.

## Basics

- Base URL: the server root; all data routes are under `/v1`.
- Auth: send `Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>` on every `/v1` request. `/openapi.json` and
  `/llms.txt` need no token.
- JSON field names are camelCase. Unknown fields are rejected (check spelling).
- IDs are prefixed ULIDs: `trip_...`, `trv_...` (traveler), `act_...` (activity).
- Every create/update returns the full updated resource, so you never need a second request.
  Deletes of trips and activities return 204.

## Time rules (important)

- Every trip has an IANA `timezone` (e.g. `Asia/Tokyo`; default `UTC`).
- Trip `startDate`/`endDate` and day `date`s are calendar days (`YYYY-MM-DD`) in the trip's
  timezone.
- Timestamps (`time.startAt`, `time.endAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`) must be sent as ISO 8601
  WITH an offset or `Z`, e.g. `2027-04-03T10:00:00+09:00` for 10:00 in Tokyo. A timestamp
  without an offset is rejected. Responses are always UTC with `Z`
  (`2027-04-03T01:00:00.000Z`); convert with the trip's timezone to show local time.
- An activity's `startAt` must fall on its day in the trip's timezone. `endAt` must be later
  (it may be after midnight).
- `daysUntilStart` is computed from today in the trip's timezone (0 on the first day,
  negative once started). Trip `status` is `upcoming`, `ongoing`, or `past`.

## Data model

A trip is a collection of days; each day holds that day's activities.

- Trip: `id, name, destination, timezone, startDate, endDate, travelers[], ownerId,
  schemaVersion, createdAt, updatedAt` (+ computed `daysUntilStart`, `status`).
- Traveler (inside a trip): `id, name, color` (`#rrggbb`; assigned from a palette if omitted).
- Day: `tripId, date, dayNumber, lodging {name} | null` (where you sleep that night),
  `startLocation {name} | null` (where the day starts), `activities[], createdAt, updatedAt`.
  There is exactly one day per date from startDate to endDate; days are created and removed
  with the trip's dates.
- Activity (always on a day): `id, tripId, date, title, status (idea|planned|done, default
  planned), time {startAt, endAt|null} | null, location {name} | null, notes | null,
  travelerIds[], createdAt, updatedAt`. `time: null` means no fixed time.

## Operations (operationId: method path)

Trips
- list_trips: GET /v1/trips?status=upcoming|ongoing|past&sort=startDate|-startDate|createdAt|-createdAt|name
- create_trip: POST /v1/trips  {name, startDate, endDate, destination?, timezone?}
- get_trip: GET /v1/trips/{tripId}
- update_trip: PATCH /v1/trips/{tripId}  (any of name, destination, timezone, startDate, endDate)
- delete_trip: DELETE /v1/trips/{tripId}  (also deletes its days and activities)

Days
- list_days: GET /v1/trips/{tripId}/days  (every day with lodging, start location, and
  activities sorted by start time)
- get_day: GET /v1/trips/{tripId}/days/{date}
- update_day: PATCH /v1/trips/{tripId}/days/{date}  {lodging?, startLocation?}  (null clears)

Travelers (each returns the updated trip)
- add_traveler: POST /v1/trips/{tripId}/travelers  {name, color?}  (new traveler is last)
- update_traveler: PATCH /v1/trips/{tripId}/travelers/{travelerId}  {name?, color?}
- remove_traveler: DELETE /v1/trips/{tripId}/travelers/{travelerId}  (also removed from activities)

Activities
- add_activity: POST /v1/trips/{tripId}/days/{date}/activities  {title, time?, location?, notes?, status?, travelerIds?}
- list_activities: GET /v1/trips/{tripId}/activities?date=&travelerId=&status=
- get_activity: GET /v1/trips/{tripId}/activities/{activityId}
- update_activity: PATCH /v1/trips/{tripId}/activities/{activityId}  (send only what changes;
  `time` and `location` are replaced whole; `null` clears time/location/notes)
- move_activity: POST /v1/trips/{tripId}/activities/{activityId}/move  {date, startAt?, endAt?}
  (date only: keeps the local times of day on the new day)
- delete_activity: DELETE /v1/trips/{tripId}/activities/{activityId}

## Common workflows

1. Plan a trip: create_trip -> add_traveler (once per person) -> update_day to set lodging for
   each night -> add_activity on each day -> list_days to review the plan.
2. Reschedule: move_activity with a new `date` (keeps times) or with `startAt`/`endAt`.
3. Mark something done: update_activity {"status": "done"}.
4. Assign people: update_activity {"travelerIds": ["trv_..."]} (IDs from get_trip).
5. Shorten a trip: move activities off the days being dropped and clear their lodging, then
   update_trip with the new dates.

## Safe concurrent edits

get_trip, get_activity, and every mutation return an `ETag` header. Send it back as
`If-Match` on a change; if someone else changed the resource meanwhile you get 412 with the
`current` version in the body. If-Match is optional.

## Errors

Errors use `application/problem+json`: `{type, title, status, detail, errors?}`. `detail` says
exactly what to fix; validation failures (422) list each `{path, message}`, e.g.
`body.time: endAt must be after startAt (got ... and ...)`. Unknown IDs give 404
naming the missing ID (a date outside the trip is a 404 too). 409 means the change conflicts
with other data: shrinking a trip would drop days that still have plans, or a new timezone
would make a timed activity start on another day. The detail lists what to fix first.
